Name: Linda
Dialog: Stop. Okay, your stories are always full of holes, but it's usually just one story. Here, let me demonstrate. I'll be the "Candace" and you will be the "beautiful mother". (Clears throat) (Imitating Candace) Mom, Phineas and Ferb have brought Genghis Khan back from the past and he's teaching the neighbors how to throw hatchets from horseback. (Normal voice) You see? One story.

Name: Linda
Dialog: He does need the exercise. Well, I'm heading to the store to pick up some things for dinner. I'm thinking spaghetti and meatballs, or a spaghetti-meatball. That's spaghetti and meat mixed up into a big ball. It's less of a choice of food than a choice of shape. Don't forget to bring a doodie bag for Perry! (leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Candace. All the times I called you delusional and mocked you to my friends behind your back, all those journals I've filled with an eye towards stand-up comedy...but you were telling the truth! (She hugs her.) I'm so sorry. You're the best daughter any mother could dream of having.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I don't know what you kids are doing, but I'm taking an online knitting test in a few minutes, and I need it to be quiet around here. (sarcastic tone) You might not remember quiet. I'm not sure you two have ever met. Anyway I'm putting you on noise patrol. You're in charge.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey hon, I was just reading this article about mothers and daughters, and really listening to your teen. And I realized I've hardly seen you all summer, so for the whole day today, it's you and me. Whatever you want to do, I'm all yours. Anything at all.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, I get it, a submarine sandwich submarine sand sculpture! You've got such special skills, sweetie! You've really outdone yourself! I'm so proud of you, and I ran into a sandcastle college recruiter who thinks he can get you a scholarship.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I'm on my way to...You know, this feels awfully familiar: I tell you I'm going out, later you'll tell me Phineas and Ferb are up to something, but there's nothing there to see, so we all have pie. Just another ordinary day.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Good for you. I would've been home sooner, but it took me an hour to drive around the road construction in the neighborhood. It sure would be helpful if they could just make the days a little longer. (chuckles) Who do I call about that?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Don't be silly, Candace. She's just a little girl. How much trouble could she be? (sees Phineas and Ferb under an out of control sprinkler) I see you've discovered the broken sprinkler. Yeah, I'd better get to the hardware store! It's beginning to look like Niagara Falls out here.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, it'll have to wait. Traffic lights are out all over the city. Of course you know I'd like nothing better than to give up my special time with your father, to run home and not see what they may, or may not have done.

Name: Linda (cont'd.)
Dialog: It makes me want to run right out and buy some tools. (Candace slowly turns her head to see the billboard has changed; her jaw drops wide in shock.) Now, if you'll excuse me, I had better get back to the attic before your father blows up another pair of... (inflatable legs burst off-screen) Oops, too late. (walks away) I'm coming, dear! And I have the patch kit.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I see your point, Candace. No crazy person would scream at a post like that. I'll be in the dairy section if you want to come yell at some cheese. (leaves, but comes back) Would you like that, honey? Would you like to yell at some cheese?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I just wanna capture these memories because you guys are growing up so fast. (Her eyes well up with tears.) No! No time for waterworks. These pictures always make me cry. I've gotta finish up so I can spend the rest of the day with you kids.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I have this weird desire to go outside. (Candace gets more nervous) Normally, around this time of day, you're pulling me to go out in the yard and I kind of have a hankering to do it! It's like a Pavlovian "go outside" response. Let's go!

Name: Linda
Dialog: (opens the door) Your father wants me to listen to one of his "soundscapes", so I figured I'd strap on the headphones and finally get those flowers planted in the backyard. Do you think you can entertain yourself up here alone?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Mostly worms and insect larvae. (Candace/Perry starts to barf then Linda puts her outside) Oh, Perry! Now I have to get the carpet cleaned again! Hey, maybe I lost my earrings when I was folding Candace's laundry. Why don't you help me look while you wait, Jeremy?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'll just leave that to the professionals at the magazine. (drives past an inflatable wading pool) Oh, look at that, an inflatable wading pool. Oh, it's just like the one I used to play in with Candace when she was little. Remember, hon?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yup. Basically, if you're really in charge, you won't need to call at all. You see, if the boys are doing something bust-worthy, that means you're not doing your job and you would be in trouble too.

Name: Linda
Dialog: If I had a nickel for every time Candace promised to show me something and nothing was there, I'd have $5.20, which isn't a lot, but it's weird that it's happened a hundred and four times, right?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, my! Look at all the fun costumes! (passing out candy) Here you go. And here's one for you. And here's one for the little princess. And one for you. Oh, but wait! Don't go away! (singsongy) We have a little surprise for you! (leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: So, what's on the list? Another day filled with big plans? (reads the list) "Herd all the nerfs into Beggar's Canyon, teach the sarlaac to brush his teeth, and giving a bantha a shower." That's awfully ambitious!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'm glad your ankle's feeling better, dear. But you should really be lying down. And look, the kids cleared out the perfect spot for my snapdragons! I think that earns you for some pie.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Dash, dot, dot, dot, dash, dash. It's a good thing that I worked on that submarine those three summers that Candace was at Morse code camp. "Boys built old-timey..." (sighs) I don't even wanna know.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (dryly) And you're not crazy because...? (Candace turns toward the post where the poster was and screams.) I see your point, Candace. No crazy person would scream at a post like that. I'll be in the dairy section if you wanna come yell at some cheese, or anything.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You're such a nice boy, Jeremy. I can see why Candace built a shrine of you in her room. (laughs) Oopsy! I probably shouldn’t have said that. Thanks for feeding Perry while I look for my earrings.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm sorry, but this is really for your own good. We need you both to understand that what you've been doing is way too dangerous. I'd never be able to live with myself if you got hurt.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (getting up with her purse) Which means back to school errands for me and making the most of the day for you. (looking at her watch) Ooh! I better get a move on. Those errands aren't gonna run themselves. (chuckles) They never do! (unenthusiastically) They never do. (leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Now you know how every year we take a family photo on the first day of summer? Well, with all the excitement of the block party, I don't want you to forget to show up for the photo.

Name: Future Linda
Dialog: Candace, my Phineas and Ferb are thirty years old now. Well, I suppose I could call them, but Phineas is in Switzerland for the award ceremony and Ferb's still in Camp David for --

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, it's a vacation. A vacation from busting. And tonight, we get to see something that only happens once a decade, the Tri-State Aurora. A natural light show in the sky.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Sorry, Candace. You've lost four phones in four months, so I got you the cheapest replacement I could find. If you lose this one, it's life without a phone for Candace Flynn. (walks away)

Name: Past Linda
Dialog: (sees the coaster) OH MY STARS! Phineas and Ferb made THAT?!? It's horribly unsafe and dangerous! (on the phone) Hello, police?! Fire department?! Army?! Air force?! Marines?! **ANYONE?!** **SAVE MY SONS!!!**

Name: Linda
Dialog: Don't just promise this time. Raise your right hand. Do you, Candace Gertrude Flynn, solemnly swear not to obsess about your brothers, or you'll suffer the Pharaoh's Curse?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Uh, which we're gonna be late for if we don't get on the road! Thanks again for looking after the kids today. Candace is skating at the park, all numbers are on the fridge.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Don't move. Hold still. (Linda takes a picture) Got it! Oh, Candace, I wouldn't have seen it, if you hadn't grabbed me forcibly, and pulled me out here. Thank you! So, you kids want some dessert?

Name: Linda
Dialog: What an active imagination you have, sweetie! Well, I think I'll leave these adorable little ragamuffins in your capable hands, Candace. I'm afraid I have to be elsewhere.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, another reject. Here you go, Perry. (turns around) Oh, there you are. What're you doing up there? (she sets the pie down and picks up what she thinks is Perry) Oh, it's a bag of bread. Haha! Oh, (rubs eyes) I've been up so long I'm starting to see things.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I still can't believe we got dinner reservations at Chez Afrique. The travel guide says it's the top romantic destination restaurant. Five star service. Panoramic views…

Name: Lindana
Dialog: Unfortunately, due to lack of evidence, it appears that Love Händel has been disqualified. So, without further ado, the winner of the award for Best Fact-Based Song is—

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hmm. It's a letter from the board of selectmen. The city council is proposing a millage to cover the overage from last quarter, and they need Phineas and Ferb's input.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Samantha, I know our book club meets tomorrow, but... The Lengthiest & Most Thorough Adventures of Lord Ramblington is really long, and I don't think I can finish it.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (putting a burnt pie on the floor by Perry) Oh, here you go, Perry. (Perry unwillingly sinks his teeth into the pie) I burnt another one. (Shot of Linda as she takes her oven mitts off. She looks rather baggy-eyed.) I guess that's what I get for staying up all night. Unless I get my act together that means plenty more for you, Perry.

Name: 80's Linda
Dialog: Maybe instead of, you know, the whole world, uh, start... small, with the Tri-State Area. (Dramatic chord plays as Heinz begins to realize what Linda told him.) Hey, the movie's starting! You have to put the speaker thing on the car.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hi, honey! I miss you. And you're missing the festivities. The boys threw me the greatest party. And Candace wrote me this really amazing song. Can you hear me?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yes. This year we've expanded our venue. We have twenty-nine varieties of meatloaf flavored ice cream, as well as various meatloaf-themed attractions and rides.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Whadaya know? It's Candace. Right on schedule. So what kind of unbelievable contraption have Phineas and Ferb built that requires me to come home immediately?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oooookay....Uh, thanks, hon. I—Oof! (She bumps into a jacket and a fedora drops onto the potted plant revealing itself to be none other than Planty the Potted Plant himself!) Oh, how cute! My new plant looks like a little secret agent! Huh. How about you guard this alcove, Mr. Secret Agent Plant. (giggles)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (with her jazz trio in a gig at Squat 'n Stitch) Testing. Welcome everyone, uh, we'll be playing some free-form jazz today. It might get a little crazy, so, hold on to those knitting needles. (Plays triangle) Hit it, girls! (Linda's trio starts playing jazz music.)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hon, the rare and elusive, bent-bill nuthatch is in its nest building season. The birds will be done traveling North, and should be right here in town today!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, the snow storm has delayed your grandparents' plane. Your father and I have to wait here at the airport until they arrive. It may be hours...

Name: Linda
Dialog: (from upstairs) Candace, I'm trying to concentrate! (going back to her computer) Now let's see: "What's the first ingredient in knitting a garment?" Oh, I know that, it's love. (types it down, only to get the wrong answer) What do you mean, "wool"?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well listen sweetie, you said so yourself, they're just plotting, right? That gives you plenty of time to go to the mall before they start implementing-guh. (makes hand gestures)

Name: Linda-2
Dialog: (opens the door) Boys, I thought you were in your room. Get inside. And get your Dooferalls back on before someone sees you. If you need me, I'll be hiding in the basement.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, perhaps we should get you a different therapist, one that won't get dragged offstage in a public meltdown. That was a lot. Are you okay, honey?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Why don't you watch some TV while you wait? Oh, hey. I've got some great baby movies of Candace. (baby cooing) Ohh! There she is in the bathtub. (bubbles gurgle) Oops! Little bubbles.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Here are your tickets for the London Eye. You might want to get in line now, 'cause it looks pretty crowded. (Carnival music) We'll pick you up around 4:15. Bye, kids.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (from inside) Enough moping around, Candace. (cut to inside Candace's room where Candace is sitting on her bed, she approaches her.) Phineas and Ferb said they've devised a fun way to wash the house. Why don't you join them? Have some fun for a change!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I mean it, Candace! You're acting really strange! (Candace dials her phone behind her back.) If I'm gonna go outside, I'm going to go outside! (The house phone rings.) Ugh, there's the phone! Hold that thought! (picks up) Hello?

Name: Linda
Dialog: That's a great idea! (she hands a stack of papers to Ferb) Here's a budget and a list of companies that do light shows. Uh, can you just handle it for me? I've gotta run. (she runs off) Thanks so much!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I seem to recall you telling me that the boys were training monkeys to juggle bicycles, and when I come home, there was a stunning lack of monkeys.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I have to say, I think Jeremy can't separate his feelings for you from his feelings for this sand castle. He must like you more than you thought...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, I'm going out. (Pulls out a coupon) I've got a coupon for a free hair styling from this new salon. I'm gonna freshen up my look. Granola bars are in the kitchen! (walks away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Ah, those corny history references made me fall for him in the first place. Vivian and I are off to our mahjong tournament. Have fun today, boys.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, put out ten, because I was talking to Jeremy's mom earlier, and we thought it would be fun to get us all together for brunch this morning.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay. (yawn) There's snacks in the sink and dishes in the fridge. I'm just gonna have some chamomile tea, which knocks me out. (goes upstairs with her teacup) So you guys have fun.

Name: Linda
Dialog: No, Candace. I just want to tell you I'm off to my book club. I left a phone number on the fridge in case of emergency. And Candace, honey...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hon, if you didn't want me to come out and spoil the surprise, you should have said so. But you are going clean up all this confetti, right?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, honey, looks like that frees you up to join me at the mall. Our trio is recording our first album today: Live at the Squat 'n' Stitch.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Oblivious) Oh, how cute. Well, I'm off for my spa day. You boys behave yourselves and don't bother your father. He's finally cleaning out the basement. (Leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Let it all out, honey. I'm relieved the other shoe has finally dropped. And you're right. It is a little sour. (takes her into the house) We should repaint the house.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (cntd) Then they throw a big diva tantrum, lose their label, and they fade to obscurity. Before you know it, their song ends up as elevator music.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You know, Candace, (turns around) most days, this is just a little disturbing. But today, with the free coupon (camera pans up) and this whole awful thing with my hair...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I have no idea what you're up to, but you're more that welcome to join us for cookies when you're done cleaning up. (At the kids) Come on kids!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Du Bois made a huge mess in the yard; they've ripped up the lawn, there's a giant bucket, and a bunch of catuses. (raises voice in an angry way) I'm so mad! I gotta go.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, honey. I'm so proud of you. I'm just going to leave the boys here to browse while I make some exchanges. (walks away) Back in a bit, working girl.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Don't play mind games with me, Candace. You're pretending to not do what I know you're actually doing won't not make me not come outside.

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's a camera, that you send away to get the film part developed, and then you take the non-film camera-only part, and you throw it away.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Actually, I just love that you kids trained poor, abandoned little squirrels and helped them get back to the wild. I am so proud of you!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I've gotta go. And just because I won't let you get pink hair, you don't have to wear some weird door. The trends these days...

Name: Linda
Dialog: (taking Candace to the side) Look Candace, most days I would humor you, but not today. I'm way too busy. Don't you have stuff of your own to do before school starts?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Now I know I have that club card in here somewhere. I always have it with me, but my purse is such a disaster area, you know how it is.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, I can see that. But, you know what, honey, as humble and gracious as you are- and I love that about you- next time, destroy him.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hi, kids! Hey! How did Crikey get here? They must've brought him in while I was at lunch. Candace, why are you sitting on a chicken?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, hey, hey! Don't let your thing with your brothers distract you! Not today! Your unlimited sandcastle potential is at stake!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Um, no, the optometrist just dilated my pupils. Everything's actually a big, blurry blob at the moment. But get me. "I'll be back!"

Name: Linda
Dialog: All set! See ya there, Candace! Okay, ladies, here I come! (She skates away) Hehehe! There I go! Ha ha! Sorry! Can't stop. FOLLOW MEEEEEEEEEEEEEE....

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Candace, it really is a lovely moon, but it's not like it was going to disappear. Couldn't it have waited till after the movie?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I was talking about your toy car!! How could you possibly think I meant my station wagon?! You are in SO much trouble, young man!!!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yes. Yes. I asked them to put something together to spice up our booth at the block party. But you can help me bring out the pies.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (on the phone) Candace, I'll see it later. Right now, I have to swing by Jeremy's uncle's restaurant and pick up some sandwiches for your father.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, keep it down! (at herself) "What do you call a clever knitter?" (pause) I know! A knit wit! Heh! Is there anything better than knitting humor?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, no. But it's sort of like shepherd's pie, except there's no potatoes or vegetables in it. You know, in the shape of a loaf.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, I'm off to Charlene's to return her cake pan. You might want to stay inside. I'm worried the heat's making you see things.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Of course you can, Dear. You can join us at the antiques symposium. This year's keynote address will debate Shellac vs. Lacquer.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Honestly, I'm kind of done here. I'm just sitting in my car at the taco shop because I like the smell. (inhales, sighs) See ya next time, Luis! (drives away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, I hope the boys don't go overboard with my present. All I'd really like is that dress from that cute little sundress shop.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hi kids, did you build a little castle? That's adorable. Candace, should I do it now? (acting) Boys! You are SO busted! Feel the burn!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm not leaving now. The girl is about to forgive the guy for the clichéd misunderstanding... (a Normbot tears through the screen) After she battles these robots.

Name: Linda
Dialog: No! (to Lawrence) Alright, well, I'm all set. I've got my lucky guitar strings, I'm wearing my lucky underwear, and, of course, I've got...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, My jazz trio has a gig at the Squat 'n Stitch today. Why don't you, Phineas and Ferb hang out at the mall together?

Name: Linda
Dialog: There, nice and clean. Ha! Now we're both a couple of good-looking dishes. Bah-da-da-duh-duh! Thank You! I'll be here all...

Name: Lindana
Dialog: I wouldn't be here without you, honey. You backed me up all the way. So it's only right that you should back me up onstage.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, kids, you're right. It does look like Niagara Falls back here. (Puts a sprinkler part on the leak.) But this part will fix that. Voila! So, who wants pie! (Everyone raises their hands and shouts.)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, Candace. You can eat the rest of that pencil. Unless you'd like to join us all for some chocolate triple layer cake.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I hate the idea of someone cutting a hole in my nice wall. Well, I can't worry about it right now. I've got music to make!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Anyway, the party looks great. But you would not believe what a long day we've had. So I think we're gonna turn in early.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (puts crown on) And because my meatloaf was voted best at the festival last year, I have the honor of being one of the judges this year.

Name: Linda
Dialog: A giant mechanical terracotta warrior? (Walking away) Really, Candace? Wouldn't that be slightly more advanced that what we have today?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (To her bird watching group) Okay gang, everyone follow me outside. The bird should be right-- (Linda gets hit with the -inator) Hey, who's ready for dessert? Doesn't that sound good?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, you can't sit inside on a gorgeous day like today. So, Missy, grab that pink bike! We're gonna get out and about!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'll just be running a few errands. First, I'll get the groceries, then to the florist, and then to the car wash.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Aww. It's nice to see Candace enjoying herself for a change. (turns to see the now empty stores) Now, where are those lemonade stands I keep hearing about?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (enters) Yeah, good luck with that. Candace, your father and I are off to the movies. While we're gone, you're in charge, okay?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, look at that giant balloon dancey-guy thing. That's really something. That's gotta be 500 feet tall. I wonder who—

Name: Linda
Dialog: (via recording) Hello, you've reached Linda Flynn-Fletcher, and if this is Candace, I'm sure what ever the boys are doing, is nothing.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'd love to, honey, but I've got quite a lot of baking to do if I wanna make my quota for the Live and Let Pie event.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm on my way to join Vivian Garcia-Shapiro, at the Mexican-Jewish Cultural Fair today. Would you like to come along?

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's beautiful! (For the rest of the scene, Candace stands completely shocked with her mouth open.) I gotta admit, I thought you were exaggerating a bit, but this is really worth getting excited about!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace I'm having a great time with you today. See how relaxing it is when you're not obsessing about your brothers? (Pause)

Name: 80's Linda
Dialog: Maybe instead of, you know, the whole world, uh, start... small, with the Tri-State Area. (dramatic chord plays) Hey, the movie's starting!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Something is very wrong. Not a single call from Candace. (Checks her phone) Not even a text message. Oga, hose me down. I'm going home.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, there's everyone. Candace, I thought you were having your dessert party today? What are you doing at Isabella's?

Name: Linda
Dialog: So I wonder what new look Bobbi has envisioned for me this time. You know, he was in my favorite band - Love Händel.

Name: Linda
Dialog: This is so exciting! (her camera beeps) Oh, I forgot to charge the battery. Oh no, I can't miss this photo op! Where is the gift shop?!

Name: Linda
Dialog: (cntd) Okay, Candace. It's your birthday, you can pick out anything you want. Ooh, what about the Mt. Rushmore bobble head?

Name: Linda
Dialog: So here's the yard. I want something nice out here. I think you know what to do. (everyone stops walking, Linda turns to landscapers) You are the landscapers after all.

Name: Linda
Dialog: That's better. (notices the billboard) Huh. I guess that is pretty scary. That guy should not be holding that wombat so close to his face.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, is everything all right? Well, if you don't even know what he's doing, how do you know if it's a problem?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I don't know how you're throwing your voice and I understand that you want attention, but I'm really, really busy.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, hey, kids. I'm going to be taking a walking tour of the Tri-State Area today. (her phone rings) Yes, Candace, you're in charge.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (lifting her blindfold) Oh my goodness! I walked all the way home? (Candace's eyes open) I guess it's hard to judge distances blindfolded. (stands up) Well, snacks anyone? (walks away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, I love it when teenagers get together and do party pranks! Do you win the game if I actually do what you say?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Wow, Jamie Oliver. I can't believe we've got one of England's most famous chefs for our little Meatloaf Festival.

Name: Linda
Dialog: It seems I spent all of last summer running around while you kids were having fun, and I missed seeing any of it.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Candace, look, there's a sandcastle building contest over there. You used to love those. You should sign up!

Name: 80's Linda
Dialog: You know, I could've gotten in the trunk, like, a block away instead of when you first picked me up at my house.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, boys, I'm off to the store for as much Mucus Be Gone as I can carry. Are you sure you're going to be okay?

Name: Future Linda
Dialog: A time machine. (Gasps) Does this mean that all those times you told me the boys were up to something, they really were?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I've got a few seconds to kill before my bladder bursts like a water balloon, so let's get this over with. (walks in the direction of the backyard, but Candace stops her)

Name: 80's Linda
Dialog: You know, I could've gotten in the trunk, like, a block away instead of when you first picked me up at my house.

Name: Linda
Dialog: The boys said they'd have fun at home so go out and do something, instead of waiting around for Jeremy to call.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh yeah! Well, that was long before you were born. It was fun, but I was happy to give it up to raise a family.

Name: Linda
Dialog: That's nice, honey. Well, the pictures should be ready soon, and then I'll see the robots when I get home. Bye. (Phone beeps)

Name: Singers and Lindana
Dialog: (Ripples back to her in the dining room, upset.) And after that, they never sing again. And no one... remembers them. (stares off into space, but quickly turns back to the boys) Not that I would know anything about that.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Now let's take these inside before the frozens turn int— (realizes the empty trunk) Oh, shoot! I must've left the other bag at the store.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (walking in with a piece of paper) Candace, oh, good, you're up. You'll have plenty of time to tackle the list of chores that you've let pile up.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Alright, alright, just as soon as I find the right sprinkler part! (hangs up) I curse the day these things were invented!

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's a journey of self-discovery while crawling around in a hole. Your dad found it on a group coupon website.

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's wonderful! (to Candace) Isn't it great? The boys are starting to take an interest in building things. (goes back into the house) Who wants stuff?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (She walks into the room) Okay Candace, I'm off to the beach. Vivian called and said the waves are crankin'. I'll have my cell with me.

Name: Future Linda
Dialog: I can't right now, dear. I'm getting ready for my tour. It's my come back, come back, come back, come back...

Name: Linda
Dialog: If it's anything like Candace's parsnip allergy, whew! I don't blame him for not wanting to appear in public.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Whalemingos, huh? Why don't you all come on in for a midnight snack. Wash your hands. Especially you, Buford.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I dunno who I should be angrier at, the Mother Mugger or whoever built that giant zoetrope. That's dangerous.

Name: Wizard (Linda)
Dialog: All this time, the boys were only trying to show you the fun way to go. The joy is in the journey, you know. (winks)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (ignores her; has her back to them, so she can't see them) My, someone's thirsty. Oh, there's more juice down here. (Bends down, revealing Candace from behind) Let's see. I've got... (bends up) pineapple, mango and tomato.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Phineas? Is that you? You sound just like Candace. I mean, you sound like you, but the things you're saying—

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, honey, Jeremy's smart enough to separate his feelings about your sandcastle from his feelings about you!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, I think they're upstairs. Can you do me a favor and take the laundry up? I'm late for an appointment.

Name: Linda
Dialog: And this fossil is the only representation of the Glichiolous species from the Jurassic era. How exciting.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (walks up) I'm afraid your plans will have to wait until after Ferb's dental appointment. (walks Ferb with her) Come on, honey, time to go!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, my daughter was supposed to... (Candace stops on the rocking chair) Oh! Kids, this is Candace. (to her daughter) Good luck. I'm off to file some cookbooks.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Jack, it sure was nice of you to show Candace and me around. This satellite stuff is very interesting.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well that's funny. I could've sworn she said backyard. Oh well. If anyone needs me, I'll be washing a ton. (laughs)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (walking through a crowd of cheering fans with foam fingers) Sorry. Excuse me. Yes, you are Number One. Excuse me. Sorry. Pardon me. Alright, alright, al... excuse me!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I know you wanna drag me into the backyard right now, Candace, but can it wait until I repot my new plant?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, look. We're all here. Why don't we all get some lunch? (leaving) I think there's a pizza place right over there.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, assuming none of that is teenage code for something I should be worried about as a parent, I'm off.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Don't you remember? The Doo Wop Hop is tonight. All the neighborhood moms have volunteered to be carhops.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, could you hold the door for me? I have to return this novelty lawn mower your father got.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'm off to my favorite author's book signing. Try not to freak out on your brothers while I'm gone.

Name: Linda
Dialog: What you need is an award-winning meatloaf. This is Nigel and Adrian, they're this year's Meatloaf Kings!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I do solemnly swear... (The house rumbles.) Do you hear that? It sounds like someone is building something, like, in our yard.

Name: Linda
Dialog: If you'll need me, I'll be in the house. But, and I mean this in the nicest way possible, don't need me. (leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Forget the boys, Candace. We're on vacation. Let's head to the spa. That'll help you, I mean us, unwind.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm a little busy here, Candace. If this is your daily call about your brothers, can I get a rain check?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You seem so different today, honey. But in a good way. Usually, you'd be trying to bust the boys by now.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Gosh, it's been so long since I've played chess. I can't remember how the knight moves. Do you remember?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I need a 25-pound tub of mayonnaise and 80 pounds of potatoes to make potato salad for the bridge club.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm really busy, so I need you to man our pie booth at all times. Do not leave under any circumstances.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I got a clue! As I was careening past her window, I saw Samantha checking movie schedules on her phone!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, more specifically, it should be right in our backyard at exactly four today! Isn't it exciting!?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, where was I? (she smells something and opens the oven to reveal smoke) Oh, no!!! (she takes out yet another burnt pie) Well, Perry, looks like you've got yourself another... Uh, where's Perry?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (overlapping) Aw, it's nice to see you giving up your obsession with the boys and getting into the spirit of things.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Not yet. Although they are trying to figure out how they can both use the push broom at the same time.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You know what, why don't you just come along so I don't spend the whole day in the teen hygiene aisle?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey, boys. I'm just working on my junk sculpture for the Modern Installations by Moms charity auction.

Name: Lindana
Dialog: Nice work, "Max." You've still got it. Though I can't say I remember you having it in the first place.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Her words sound funny because she has a dental instrument in her mouth) Oh, you have got to be kidding me! If you hadn't noticed, I'm kind of in the middle of something here!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Good morning, sunshine! What's your plan for today, besides, of course, padding up my cell phone bill?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (tries to climb the stairs) You know, Candace, this is the second time I've climbed up there! I'm already down half a dress size!

Name: Linda
Dialog: This is probably illegal. (looks down) Those roses really do look good. (gasps) Artificial? No. One bust at a time, Linda.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You know the driver's manual by heart, and your dad and the boys have been helping you parallel park.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You're right, Candace. There is a "giant ball of water". Though most people prefer to call it a lake. (walks away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Magnificent! Thanks for making sure I didn't miss it, dear. A perfect end to our mother-daughter day.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Wait. Nigel and Adrian are...? Are you sure? They're not tiny. And, come on, you're not even cowboys.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You know, Candace, you're gonna have to clean all this up. Mom suit. I swear. (walks off) I'm not even gonna ask.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Point taken. Okay honey, I'm off to help Dad at the antique store. Oh, hey, here's a package for you.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I don't know why you're making me do this, Candace. I mean, when do I ever dress this fancy anyways?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (offscreen) Candace, you know Wednesday is my Famous Statues Life Drawing class. (she is dressed as the Statue of Liberty) This had better be important...

Name: Linda
Dialog: (standing up) Oh, these teenagers and their slang. (walking towards the open garage door and Candace notices something about her) I'd better go run my errands. They're not gonna run themselves. (turns around and grabs her purse, revealing she's wearing cargo shorts)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Candace, honey, I don't think... You poor thing. (pauses; sighs and looks to the heavens) Forgive me, boys. What are your brothers up to?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, the yard looks great. Come on in the kitchen. I've got a plate of cake that needs cleaning up.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Your even tone and relaxed phone manner, while unsettling, are a real welcome change of pace, dear.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, I see what you mean, Candace. The natural beauty of the Unpainted Desert is like a work of art!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, but let me go upstairs first to see myself in the full-length mirror. This is just too funny.

Name: Linda
Dialog: That does seem to be a pattern, doesn't it? Come on! Enjoy the festival! Here, have a dreidel-raca!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Omigosh, I never realized that. Okay, bye. (takes out earbuds) Sorry, honey. Your dad called with an antique emergency.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Wow, this restaurant is really out of the way. I bet you can see the entire savannah from up there.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Aw, you know he's saying, "You guys are the best!" Now, come on everyone. Inside for some lemonade.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey, sweetheart. Oh, look at your outfit! Hey, guess what? We won! (flatly) But the grand prize was a star.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, you know, we do have a nice backyard. (At this point, Candace opens her eyes) Although, I never noticed that cheese smell before. (walks away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, she's still getting ready. You know girls. Have a seat. While you wait, I'll make you a snack. (sits on the couch, sees Candace/Perry underneath)

Name: Linda
Dialog: So, Dad, like, don't forget Mom's birthday is, like, coming up and, like, what she really wants...

Name: Wizard (Linda)
Dialog: On the nosy. Loosen up, sweetheart. Remember to have fun along the way. Summer won't last forever.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (from the phone) Candace, that was the supermarket. I left my pocketbook there. I'm gonna run over and pick it up.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, I love you, but you couldn't have chosen a worse moment to go completely bonkers!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I can tell. Well, if you're just gonna sit inside today, you should at least do a little reading.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, what a great day. Not one phone call from Candace with some crazy, unbelievable story about–

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm starting to get the hang of it. I think this motion refers to the swaying of the palm trees.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You don't need me to see anything today. Dad's recruited the kids to help him build a bookshelf.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, at first, I thought Du Bois were the world's worst landscapers, but they're growing on me.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, apparently, you just put some dirt in a pot. I don't know why I cleared my whole schedule.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You remember that whole stress relief thing I mentioned earlier? You might wanna look into that.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (oblivious) Not right now, sweetie. I'm going to the gardening store. Something's been eating my hydrangeas.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Just a sec, Candace. Let me grab these groceries. (As the giant building narrowly misses them as it rotates over them.) Aaand...there we go. Now what were you saying?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm going to get my hair done. I'll be back at 2. Maybe you can figure it out before I get home. (She drives off)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey, Candace. I was just heading out to Margie's baby shower and look what I found on the stoop.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (on the phone) Where are you, Candace? You promised you'd help frost the cake after you got Phineas's present.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, they really did believe they had permission. I suppose it was all a big misunderstanding.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Arranging the groceries into a shelf) No, not Doonkelberry Pie. Everybody's out of Doonkelberries! I can't find them anywhere lately.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (opens the door to her room) And the whole Tri-State Area knows you're here, Candace! Again, could you please keep it down?! (closes door)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (sarcastically) Oh my. That sounds exciting. I'll come have a look, as soon as I'm done doing whatever this is.

Name: Lindana
Dialog: (offscreen) The second nominee in the fact-based song category are the Hockey Hooligans with "Hockey Z-9".

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Phineas starts creating the checklist offscreen) Well, a musical act (Flashes back to a time when Linda was known as a singer named Lindana.) goes to the top of the charts with a catchy tune and meaningless lyrics...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, this isn't another rant about some imaginary thing your brothers are building, is it?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, if you're feeding the geese again, I hope you're not wearing a tube top. (Hangs up, then looks at her husband, who is once again the source of the whirring noise) Do you mind?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, Candace, you were right about Phineas and Ferb this whole time. We should've believed you.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, no. I'm late for my introduction to ice sculpture. (Writes a note and goes outside to Candace sleeping on the hammock) I suppose there's no need to wake her. (puts the note on her head, then leaves)

Name: Future Linda
Dialog: Candace, you're a grown woman. I really thought you had finally moved past all this nonsense.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Can you please go out on the lake with the boys to make sure they don't get into any trouble?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You again? Ha! Looks like I took you on a little trip. (opens her window) Get back to your family, little fella.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, laundry. Sometimes, I feel like our first president, because I'm washing a ton. (laughs) Ah, yeah.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Of course! Candace, Glenda was the first female train conductor in the entire Tri-State Area!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, I guess I'll just call the -- (her keys land in her hand, followed by the man and woman behind her) Oh, for goodness sake! They were in my hand the whole time!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'm heading to the beach now with my famous sub sandwiches. I'll see ya there, winner!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, I'm fine. I don't remember how I got here, but I'm glad to see you guys. All you guys!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'll tell you what, how about you shop for your own things and then meet me at the register?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well everyday is eventful in the emergency room. Candace, you really should be more careful.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, why are you dressed like that? I told you, you're going to get a heatstroke!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey! That's my umbrella! It's the Danville Mother Mugger! How do you even know I'm a mother?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey! It's the tortoise I saw earlier. Isn't that the most outrageous thing you've ever seen?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Never really noticed that, no. But, honey, don't you want me to look in the backyard to see—

Name: Linda
Dialog: Uh-huh? Uh-huh. That would count as dangerous. But I can't go anywhere until I find my keys.

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's so great when something nice happens to you, especially when you weren't expecting it. (exits)

Name: Linda
Dialog: You mean, obsessively trying to bust your brothers for their mystery crimes? Is that "fun"?

Name: Lindana
Dialog: (also bends down) ...the fact-based song category is, Slamm Hammer, with their hit, "Trees are Made of Wood".

Name: Linda
Dialog: That squirrel man dropped his hat. I should return it. I wonder what's he's doing up there.

Name: Chief Linda
Dialog: If you're gonna try and sell me another fairy tale about Ohio Flynn and Rhode Island Flet--

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, why can't you just relax, and let your brothers enjoy their do-nothing day?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You know, you could get up and walk five feet and change the channel the old-fashioned way.

Name: Linda
Dialog: It's a protective collar. The vet says that Perry needs to wear it for the rest of the day.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Why don't you come in for some snacks, kids? And if you see your dad, tell him to join us.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, Candace. Calm down. I'll come by and see you as soon as I'm done with the exchanges.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I've got a few errands to run. But I should be there by the time the contest starts.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Think of it this way, Candace: the faster I shop, the sooner I come home to bust the boys.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Cute. Okay, here's some quarters for the arcade. I'm gonna see what's keeping your sister.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Suddenly I feel like dancing. (Stops the car at the Flynn-Fletcher house and heads to the backyard; The studio and the crowd conga their out of the backyard, much to Candace's surprise.) Well, I'm here. Now, where's this "giant, animation studio"?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, look! They made a boat. It's actually waterproof and everything. That's pretty cool!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, wow! It's our house! (the screen shows the empty backyard and the kids) And you can see the boys! And their little skateboards! (waves) Hi, boys!

Name: Linda
Dialog: (takes off her cucumber slices) Candace, do you even hear the words that come out of your mouth? (puts back on the cucumber slices) You need to relax, honey.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Dink Winkerson? Disturbingly UV-sensitive host of Danville Today? But why steal umbrellas?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I thought you wanted to be the first of your friends to have a driver's license.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Boys, I'm off to Bobbi's. If you need anything, your father's inside watching television.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, and Ferb, you left your pen on the kitchen table. Have fun today, I'll be back later.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (offscreen) In the kitchen!! (Candace walks off. Cut to the kitchen to reveal groceries all over the floor.) When I said, "throw these in the kitchen," I didn't mean it literally!!!

Name: Linda
Dialog: What are all these people doing on our street? Hey! Candace. Honey, what's going on here?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, hi kids. I wanna thank you for being so quiet all afternoon... (at Candace, who opens her eyes; angrily) Unlike someone I know!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, how about ski camp on Hoth? Don't you boys ever want to see the rest of the galaxy?

Name: Linda
Dialog: But now I'm clean, so no harm done. And I can see that you're dying to tell me something.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hmm. All right. (Presses another remote, ejecting a CD) Wait. 'Kay, that's not it. Um, is it this one? No, this is another phone.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You volunteered to read to the kids' book club today, while I help reorganize cookbooks.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Wow, I've really got a knack for this modern art stuff. I need to go get more materials! (drops the blowtorch; runs off)

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm sorry, Candace. I got stuck in a bit of traffic, but I'll be there as soon as I can.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hey boys, want some fat-free whole-grain granola bars? They're still warm from the oven.

Name: Linda
Dialog: But I've always suspected Samantha doesn't read the books even though she says she does.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, is this some kind of ridiculous internet prank?! It's like, a thousand o'clock!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, it turns out your father is the one responsible for this—Hold on, is it...buzzing?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Looks out the window) Candace, you obviously have some issues with the driveway. I'm just gonna park in front. (Backs away to the front of the house. The ray fires, and the ride come back)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, watch this. I was just looking at this plate, and I said, "There, nice and..."

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, hmmm... (gasps) The book spine is barely cracked and the bookmark is only a few pages in.

Name: Linda
Dialog: There. Take it away, guys. That junk sculpture should bring in big bids at the auction. (climbs down the flatbed)

Name: Linda
Dialog: I wonder what will be waiting for me today. An invisible thing or a non-existent thing?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (to Candace) I'll be waiting over at the park till your test is over. Break a leg, sweetheart! Mwah!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, you need to lighten up a little. Take it easy. Do you know what I do to relax?

Name: Wizard (Linda)
Dialog: Oops, that's the oven. Boys, can you hand out the gifts while I check on the casserole?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (on phone) I need your help with these pies. I'm so tired I'm starting to see the weirdest things.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace Flynn, what has gotten into you?! (Candace is grabbing onto Mrs. Johnson's head with her feet to keep herself from floating.) I want the truth, and nothing but the truth!

Name: Linda
Dialog: I certainly did. (Candace giggles under) What are all my good guest towels doing out here? And they're filthy!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, I thought I told you to take that garbage out. You are so busted, young lady.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Um, honey, I gotta go. No- B-Big chef. Big meat tenderizer in front of mommy. Bye bye.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Yeah, well; gotta run. Margie won't stay pregnant forever. Don't forget to feed Perry.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Lawrence, can you look at these tile samples with me? I want to re-do the living room.

Name: Linda
Dialog: How could I miss it? But I don't understand. How the...? Or who the...? B-- What the?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, kids. Pie's almost ready. Anybody want some fresh orange juice in the meantime?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Phineas, Ferb. I'm gonna go pick up a few things. You boys stay out of trouble, okay?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Phineas, Ferb! I'm gonna go pick up a few things. You boys stay out of trouble, okay?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You surprised me, Lawrence. I thought you were gonna sit in front of this TV all day.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Alright, Candace. So what was it you wanted to show me? (Invention lands.) Holy guacamole! What is that?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Cheer up, guys. I'm sure you'll have a fun day anyway. (She and Lawrence leave the kitchen) Bye, kids, be good. Have fun!

Name: Linda
Dialog: She always calls before the best part of the song. (answers) Yes, dear. What can I do for you?

Name: Linda
Dialog: The boys are here, too? Hon, I'm boxed in. I've got a heck of a line in front of me.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, this is a dandruff commercial. Is there something you're trying to tell me?

Name: Linda (cont'd.)
Dialog: (offscreen) You guys made the lawn look great! (Candace opens her eyes and turns her head, realizing the gorge disappeared.) Oh, it's all weeded and watered... Oh, well done!

Name: Linda
Dialog: (stops what she is doing) Baljeet picking on Buford? Candace, Buford outweighs Baljeet by like, 90 hamburgers!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Honey, normally, I'd prefer you put this energy into something more... productive...

Name: Linda
Dialog: Sweetie, I went through a similar phase when I was your age. Try writing some poems.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You were driving a full-sized car?! Oh, that's it, young lady! You're **grounded!**

Name: Linda
Dialog: (places hand on forehead) Candace, I- look- call me back in a few minutes. I'm a little ticked off right now.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh my gosh. That is the cutest thing I've ever seen. Everyone say "Canadian bacon!"

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I guess that answered the inflatable legs question. (at Candace) Now, what is it, Candace?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You're a laugh riot, Candace. (starts to leave) Think you can handle watching Phineas and Ferb today?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I'm at least glad to see you kids are going to finish up my leftover biryani.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (sighs) You wait so long to hear your baby say the word and then they never stop saying it.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You're right! It's beautiful! (hugs her) Happy birthday, honey. (Kisses Candace's cheek) Now let's go find your father. (She walks away)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, he doesn't sound well enough to travel, hon. Maybe we should leave him at home.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Great job fixing the ship, honey. (Cut to reveal the sloop is still on the rock.) But how are we going to get it back in the water?

Name: Linda
Dialog: You can do this, Candace! Just look into the turn and ease your foot off the brake.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Everything okay, Candace? Y'know, you really shouldn't have drinks in the library.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, for us? That is so nice. And Candace, so responsible. Not a single phone call.

Name: Linda
Dialog: We'll be barbecuing steaks for the whole neighborhood! Why don't you bring Jeremy?

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm sorry, Candace. Now I know all the crazy exploits you told me about were true.

Name: Linda and Candace
Dialog: (Linda getting up with her purse) Which means back to school errands for me and making the most of the day for you.

Name: Linda
Dialog: No one is going anywhere until we figure out what this is and where it came from!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, seriously, isn't Phineas a little young to be a roller coaster engineer?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Voicemail recording) Hi, this is Mom. Leave your psychotic rant about the boys when you hear the beep. (Phone beeps)

Name: Linda
Dialog: I want you boys to pick out some nice back-to-school clothes. (Phineas, Ferb, Linda, and Perry enters the store, and presently walk back out) Wow, that was fast.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Well, I expect you to be home by the time I get back to help put everything away!

Name: Linda
Dialog: Phineas, Ferb? I'll be over at Vivian's house for a few hours. You kids have fun.

Name: Linda
Dialog: What is it Candace? (Candace asks something) No, I don't know what Ferb Latin is. (sighs) Give me fifteen minutes.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (On phone) Candace, honey, I'm at the car-wash, and I'll be heading home very soon. Bye bye.

Name: Linda
Dialog: The same old routine every day. Doesn't it ever get--" mm, I don't know-- boring?

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Going down the stairs) Great! I'll meet you at the gift shop, Dear. I still have to buy that big stick.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (turning, just as Phineas and Ferb's floats leave) Okay you want me to turn around? I'm turning around. Can we just eat lunch now?!

Name: Linda
Dialog: That's quite a racket back there. Are you sure you don't want me to take a look?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, seriously, isn't Phineas a little young to be a rollercoaster engineer?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, did you say you were doing a Perry movie? This I have to see. I'm on my way. (She drives off.)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Reverse psychology. Nice try, hon. Glad to see you changing it up. See ya later.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay, there's been no change in the last ten minutes. I should call your father.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I just feel so bad we missed the video presentation while we were at the bakery.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (Churning butter) Oh, these new gadgets are so complicated. Up and down, and up and down, and up–-

Name: Lindana
Dialog: I'm sorry, kids. The journal isn't good enough. You need actual, physical proof.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Uh, Lawrence, what's going on here? I've seen you put on more shirts than that.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, honey, I think it's time to get you out of the sun for a little while. (she and Isabella lead Candace away.)

Name: Linda
Dialog: Excellent, we have an understanding. Now go to bed. You can try again tomorrow. (She leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm sure your mom let you go to a concert by yourself when you were a teenager.

Name: Linda
Dialog: You think you feel ridiculous? I'm carrying a jackalope into a lawnmower store.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (She looks through the telescope, but the water blocks the action) Oh, Old Reliable Geyser. How exciting! (at Candace) I'm just gonna go back to the gift shop.(Candace looks through the telescope, the water has halted gushing. Candace cringes and stomps off, causing the telescope to bounce up to Perry, who enters Lincoln's head to Doofenshmirtz's lair)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (angrily) Candace, I've been waiting at the checkout line for a half hour, where are you?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Candace, is this a ploy to get me to go outside to see what the boys are up to?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh, great. I wish you could teleport to where my earrings are. I've lost them.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Hi, boys! (at Candace, sternly) If you'll excuse me, Candace, I'm gonna get back for the second set. (leaves)

Name: Linda
Dialog: (looks at her list) Oh, I guess I did. (gives Candace some bags) Alright, throw these in the kitchen and I'll be right back.

Name: Linda
Dialog: I have time to do nice things when I'm not distracted by panicked phone calls.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Why do I feel that all of this has something to do with busting your brothers?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Finally getting 'round to spring cleaning in the summer. First up, the fridge.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Okay Candace honey. Oh, would you take the garbage out? It's over by the door.

Name: Linda
Dialog: Your father and I are looking forward to the Annual Couple's Surfing Contest.

Name: Linda
Dialog: (taking Candace off to the side) Look, Candace. Most days, I would humor you, but not today. I'm way too busy—

Name: Linda
Dialog: I'm sure it's going to be all right, dear, but, who are "Phineas" and "Ferb"?

Name: Linda
Dialog: So you could look down on anybody's backyard and just see what they're doing?

Name: Linda
Dialog: Oh Candace, revel in your brothers' imagination. Makes life so much more fun.

Name: Linda
Dialog: OH! I'll just order a pizza! All right, Candace, let's see what you've got...

Name: Linda
